Article Title: MP Pappu Yadav attacked at home during presser
Article Text:
The attack is believed to be linked to Yadav’s recent skit outside Parliament over the alleged donation theft at the Ayodhya Ram temple.

NEW DELHI: High drama unfolded at the New Delhi address of Independent MP Pappu Yadav Sunday after a man allegedly threw a slipper at him and another allegedly brandished a knife when he was holding a news conference.The accused, identified by sources as Sumit and Happy Sharma, are from Bulandshahr in UP. Police have detained Sumit (34), and are probing Happy’s role. They are verifying if Happy was the one who threw a slipper at the MP, and if Sumit, who runs a hardware shop, brandished a knife at the event.The attack is believed to be linked to Yadav’s recent skit outside Parliament over the alleged donation theft at the Ayodhya Ram temple. On July 31, Opposition MPs staged a skit outside Parliament to protest on the issue, during which Yadav, dressed as a priest, was seen putting donation money in his pocket. MP Bansuri Swaraj complained to police Saturday on the matter.Sunday’s videos show someone throwing a slipper at Yadav. Moments later, chaos erupts and chairs fly as supporters rush to overpower the men, and police step in. Members of Yadav’s team displayed before reporters the slipper and a knife which, they alleged, were used in the attack.Yadav alleged that it was a planned attempt on his life. “When the knife was drawn to attack, our supporters and associates tried to restrain the assailant. I stepped forward and positioned myself between the attacker and Pappu Yadav, and I was beaten severely as a result,” Zaid, MP Yadav’s media convener, claimed.Happy told reporters that the duo was “not carrying a knife or any other weapon. We were allowed inside only after a security check.” Police, however, have found a knife in Sumit's possession.Advocate Kanishk Arora, of Yadav’s legal team, said the MP had received death threats in the past several days, including videos on social media announcing cash rewards for killing him and threatening his family. “We had informed Delhi Police about the threats and sought enhanced security ahead of Sunday’s news conference. However, only three police personnel were deployed,” Arora said.
Article Summary: The attack is believed to be linked to Yadav’s recent skit outside Parliament over the alleged donation theft at the Ayodhya Ram temple. Yadav, dressed as a priest, was seen putting donation money in his pocket in the skit. Police have detained Sumit (34), and are probing Happy's role.

NEW DELHI: DMK Sunday mounted a furious pushback against Rahul Gandhi's describing any support to govt's widely speculated move to revive the bill to increase Lok Sabha's strength, coupled with delimitation of constituencies, as a betrayal of Tamil Nadu amid buzz in political circles that the regional party may come around to backing the measure.A day after Rahul, during his visit to Tamil Nadu, said any party supporting the constitution amendment bill in Parliament will be a 21st century Ettappan, a historical figure reviled for treachery, senior DMK MP Dayanidhi Maran came out with a blistering retort. Those who only talk about irregularities in the exam, rather than insisting on completely abolishing NEET are traitors. Those who condemn BJP's horse-trading but ignore TVK's disgusting horse-trading are merely continuing that betrayal."

Article Title: 'Cancel JPSC exam': Jharkhand students continue protest, seek CBI investigation
Article Text:
For many of the young demonstrators, the protest has become a struggle over fairness and opportunity rather than merely an examination dispute

NEW DELHI: Hundreds of students continued their protest in Ranchi on Sunday for the fifth consecutive day over alleged irregularities in the 14th Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) examination, the JSSC-CGL and other recruitment tests. The demonstrators are seeking a CBI probe into recruitment examinations, cancellation of the 14th JPSC Combined Preliminary Test and reforms in the state’s recruitment agencies.The protestors escalated their agitation with a torchlight procession and threatened to march to the Jharkhand Assembly if the state government does not address their demands.The students, who are holding an indefinite sit-in at Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium, marched to Albert Ekka Chowk on Sunday evening, raising slogans against the JMM-led alliance government and demanding an impartial investigation into the alleged irregularities in the JPSC and JSSC examinations.They warned that if the government failed to respond in the coming days, they would march to the Jharkhand Assembly and stage a gherao.“We have been holding protests, but no government officials approached us to listen to our concerns on these issues. This clearly shows the insensitivity of this JMM-led alliance government towards the thousands of students and youths of the state,” the protesters alleged.The demonstration began on July 29 and has since drawn support from students across Jharkhand, many of whom say years of preparation for competitive examinations are being undermined by repeated allegations of paper leaks and irregularities.At the protest site, students continued raising slogans such as “Order CBI probe in JPSC”, “Long live Students Unity” and “Shame on Hemant Soren”.“Paper leaks in JPSC have happened several times. This time, OMR sheets of candidates have been leaked. Chief Minister Hemant Soren has ordered a CID probe, but we are not satisfied,” JPSC aspirant Rahul Kumar Kranti said.He alleged that previous investigations into the Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission CGL paper leak had not resulted in action and claimed that the latest probe could also be “covered up” after a few months.“We have completely lost faith in the ongoing CID probe. We demand a CBI probe into all recruitment examinations conducted by the JPSC and JSSC over the past seven years. We also demand the chief minister’s resignation on moral grounds,” Kranti said.The protesters are demanding cancellation of the 14th JPSC Combined Preliminary Test held on April 19 and an independent investigation by central agencies, including the CBI and the Enforcement Directorate, into alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations conducted by the JPSC and JSSC. They are also seeking the introduction of a fifth option of “not attempted” in OMR sheets.For many of the young demonstrators, the protest has become a struggle over fairness and opportunity rather than merely an examination dispute.“The careers of thousands of students and aspirants are at stake due to corruption in both agencies. Most of us come from farmers’ families. We only want fair opportunities based on merit,” said Ankit Kumar from Giridih district.Sneha, a tribal student from Ranchi, said protesters wanted strict punishment for those involved in the alleged irregularities and cancellation of the 14th JPSC examination.“I have been preparing for competitive examinations since 2023. But if an equal and fair chance is not given, how can I get a job? I urge CM Soren to listen to our demands,” she said.Archana Kumari from Palamu said the students would continue their agitation until the government addressed their demands and fixed accountability for the alleged irregularities.Despite days of protest, students said they were determined to continue their sit-in, with volunteers and supporters from different parts of the country helping sustain the demonstration.“The state government is still in a sleeping mode. We are getting support from across the country. People from various cities are sending food items to the protest site. We are thankful to those helping us continue our protest,” said Shyam Bihari Gupta, a student from Balumath in Latehar district.
Article Summary: Hundreds of students continued their protest in Ranchi on Sunday for the fifth consecutive day over alleged irregularities. Demonstrators are seeking a CBI probe into recruitment examinations, cancellation of the 14th JPSC Combined Preliminary Test and reforms in the state’s recruitment agencies.

Article Title: '2024 movement fooled Bangladesh': Taslima Nasreen's 'lesson' warning over Delhi student protests

NEW DELHI: Exiled Bangladeshi author Taslima Nasreen on Sunday said the student movement that led to the ouster of Sheikh Hasina ’s government had “fooled us”, drawing a parallel between the protests in Bangladesh and the recent student demonstrations in Delhi.Speaking to reporters in Kolkata two days after returning to the city for the first time since 2007, the acclaimed writer acknowledged that she had not followed the Delhi protest closely, but added that a short video clip from the agitation “reminded me of the July 2024 students’ movement in Bangladesh.”"That student movement in Bangladesh fooled us. Because we thought the students wanted to abolish the quota system. Sheikh Hasina had also agreed to their demands, but ultimately the government fell. Later, we found that jihadis (Islamic fundamentalists) were behind that movement. The fallout has not been good for Bangladesh. Jihadis have taken over power there," she told reporters.Nasreen, who left Bangladesh in 1994 following threats from Islamic radicals over her work, further stated that the developments in her home country had “reinforced” her concerns about the consequences of such movements.The 63-year-old author added that the 2024 Bangladesh protests should “therefore serve as a lesson.”Nasreen’s remarks came ahead of the second anniversary of Sheikh Hasina’s resignation on August 5. The former prime minister has been living in exile in New Delhi.The Awami League government was replaced by an interim administration led by Nobel laureate Muhammad Yunus three days after Sheikh Hasina’s ouster.In February this year, the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) secured a sweeping victory in a landmark parliamentary election, paving the way for party chairperson Tarique Rahman to become the new prime minister.The protests in Delhi were held demanding the resignation of then Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan over the NEET (UG) paper leak issue and seeking broader examination reforms. After more than five weeks of an indefinite sit-in led by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) in the national capital, Pradhan resigned on July 25, bringing the agitation to an end.
Article Summary: Exiled Bangladeshi author Taslima Nasreen draws parallel between Bangladesh and Delhi student protest. Nasreen: "That student movement in Bangladesh fooled us. Because we thought the students wanted to abolish the quota system. Later, we found that jihadis (Islamic fundamentalists) were behind that movement"

Article Title: ‘Ban on Sheikh Hasina’s Awami League a move against democracy’: Taslima Nasreen
Article Text:
Sheikh Hasina; Taslima Nasreen

Nasreen backs Uniform Civil Code , calls it necessary for women's equality

(With ANI inputs)

NEW DELHI: Exiled Bangladeshi author Taslima Nasreen on Sunday criticised the ban on former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina’s Awami League party, calling it a "move against democracy” and expressing uncertainty over Hasina’s return to the country.“No political party should be banned. The manner in which Sheikh Hasina was forced to leave the country is questionable. It was not right to ban the Awami League. It was a move against democracy. I want the ban to be lifted as soon as possible,” Nasreen told reporters at a press conference in Kolkata.Sheikh Hasina has been living in Delhi since August 5, 2024, after resigning as prime minister following weeks of student-led protests. The interim government led by Nobel laureate Muhammad Yunus, which took charge after the fall of the Awami League administration, banned the party in May 2025 under anti-terrorism laws.Meanwhile, Nasreen alleged that several Awami League workers had been tortured and killed during Sheikh Hasina’s exile and expressed uncertainty over whether the former prime minister would be able to return to Bangladesh.“Many Awami League workers were tortured and murdered. Sheikh Hasina wants to return, but I do not know whether that will be possible.But no one wants me to go back,” she said.Nasreen also criticised Jamaat-e-Islami, now Bangladesh's principal opposition party, accusing it of opposing women’s equality and seeking the imposition of Sharia law.“Now we have Jamaat-e-Islami as an opposition party. It is against women’s equality, and they want Sharia rule. If that happens, no minority will survive. Bangladesh is moving towards darkness. No one is trying to civilise Bangladesh. The government is only trying to remain in power,” she added.The 63-year-old author further claimed that “hatred against Hindus” was being spread in some madrasas and mosques in Bangladesh.“In many madrasas and mosques, hatred is being taught against Hindus,” Nasreen remarked.Turning to the issue of the Uniform Civil Code (UCC), Nasreen said she had been advocating for such a law for the past 40 years and described it as essential in any “civilised country”.“I have been fighting for the UCC for the past 40 years. This is much needed in any civilised country,” she remarked.She claimed that religious laws continued to affect women’s rights in Bangladesh, alleging that Hindu women in the country lacked adequate legal protections, including the right to divorce.“In Bangladesh, Hindu girls have no rights; they do not even have the right to divorce. Due to religious laws, women are suffering. Hindus are being tortured in Bangladesh. During the Yunus regime, Hindus were tortured even more,” she alleged.In July, the BJP-led West Bengal government constituted a nine-member expert committee headed by retired Supreme Court judge Justice Ranjana Prakash Desai to examine and finalise a draft UCC for the state. The state government plans to introduce the legislation during the upcoming August Assembly session.Nasreen, who has lived in exile since 1994, when she was forced to leave Bangladesh due to the threat from Islamic radicals over her work, returned to Kolkata nearly two decades. She was forced to leave the city in 2007 following protests over her writings and memoir Dwikhandito (Split into Two), published in 2003.
Article Summary: Sheikh Hasina has been living in Delhi since August 5, 2024, after resigning as prime minister following weeks of student-led protests. The interim government led by Nobel laureate Muhammad Yunus, which took charge after the fall of the Awami League administration, banned the party in May 2025 under anti-terrorism laws.

Article Title: 'Kerala stands united': Rahul Gandhi offers support as rains claim 8 lives, leave 8 missing
Article Text:
Heavy rainfall wrecks havoc in Kerala, Rahul Gandhi offers support

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Sunday expressed deep sorrow over the devastation caused by heavy rains in Kerala, offering condolences to the families of eight people who lost their lives and urging party workers to assist in relief and recovery operations."Deeply saddened by the devastation caused by heavy rains across Kerala. My heartfelt condolences to the families of the eight people who have lost their lives. May those still missing be found safe, and the injured make a swift recovery," he said in a post on X.The Congress leader also added that the state government was making every possible effort to support affected families and coordinate relief operations. "I urge all Congress workers and volunteers to assist these efforts in every possible way," he said, urging people to remain vigilant, especially in hilly regions, and follow authorities' guidance."Kerala stands united in this difficult hour. I stand firmly with every affected family," Rahul Gandhi added.Kerala chief minister V D Satheesan confirmed that eight people have died, an equal number are missing and 13 others injured in the heavy rains that triggered landslides, waterlogging and property damage across the state. In a statement, he said 27 houses were completely destroyed, 196 homes partially damaged and 5,792 people have been shifted to 209 relief camps.Satheesan said that despite a reduction in rainfall, people should remain vigilant, especially in hilly areas. He said the government would ensure assistance to families of the deceased and those who lost homes and livelihoods.Revenue minister A P Anilkumar told reporters the situation was improving and was under control. He said damaged roads had been restored in many areas, though some restrictions on vehicular movement remained. He added that alerts had been issued for several districts and preparations were in place.According to the Kerala State Disaster Management Authority, the state received up to 320 mm of rainfall in some parts on Saturday, with Ayyankunnu in Kannur district recording the highest. The rains inundated low-lying and riverside areas, especially in Pathanamthitta, Idukki, Wayanad, Kottayam, Kozhikode and Kannur districts.IMD issued an orange alert for 12 districts and a yellow alert for Thiruvananthapuram and Kollam, warning of flash floods in all districts between 2 pm and 8 pm. Heavy rainfall was predicted on August 2, 3 and 6, with strong winds of up to 50 kmph.The Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services warned of huge waves of 2.7 to 3.5 meters along the northern Kerala coast and advised fishermen and coastal residents to be vigilant.On Sunday morning, while rains subsided, water had not receded from flooded areas, with people seen travelling using small boats. The water level in some power generation dams in Idukki, Pathanamthitta and Thrissur districts remained in red alert status, according to KSDMA.State tourism minister P C Vishnunadh said an additional NDRF team was deployed for rescue efforts in Pathanamthitta and Aranmula, with fire force units from Thiruvananthapuram, Palakkad and Ernakulam. Fishermen and fishing boats were also deployed for quick response.
Article Summary: Rahul Gandhi expresses deep sorrow over devastation caused by heavy rains in Kerala. He offers condolences to the families of eight people who lost their lives and urges party workers to assist in relief and recovery operations. Kerala chief minister V D Satheesan confirmed that eight people have died, an equal number are missing.

NEW DELHI: Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) president Mayawati on Sunday announced the expulsion of former Rajya Sabha member Ashok Siddarth from the party, less than a year after re-inducting him in September 2025.Mayawati said Siddarth had been expelled with immediate effect in the interest of the party and its movement, adding that he would not be re-inducted in the future."In the interest of the party and the movement, Ashok Siddarth has been expelled from the BSP with immediate effect and will not be taken back into the party in future," the former Uttar Pradesh chief minister wrote on X.Explaining the decision, Mayawati noted that Siddarth had earlier been expelled over "indiscipline" during the Maharashtra assembly elections, particularly over issues related to coordination with the party's state unit in ticket distribution.Mayawati added that Siddharth was subsequently entrusted with organisational responsibilities in states outside Uttar Pradesh to help strengthen the party's base. However, despite repeated warnings, complaints of indiscipline and violation of party directives continued to surface from Karnataka, Odisha and West Bengal, she alleged.The BSP supremo also clarified that the ex-Rajya Sabha MP had been relieved of all party responsibilities on Saturday.She further alleged that rumours about his possible return to Uttar Pradesh were being deliberately spread to create confusion within the organisation and derail the BSP's preparations for the next Uttar Pradesh assembly elections.Siddarth, the father-in-law of Mayawati's nephew Akash Anand, was previously expelled from the BSP in February last year over alleged "anti-party" activities.According to Mayawati, Siddharth was re-inducted after he assured the leadership that such lapses would not be repeated.The BSP chief also announced the expulsion of party coordinator Randhir Singh Beniwal on charges of indiscipline and violation of party directives.According to Mayawati, Beniwal had been entrusted with organisational responsibilities in Punjab, Himachal Pradesh and Jammu and Kashmir.She also announced that Rajya Sabha MP Ramji Gautam, who was assigned fresh responsibilities in the party's recent national-level organisational reshuffle, would continue as the BSP's in-charge for Punjab, along with other states, until the Punjab assembly elections next year and the Lok Sabha polls in 2029.Mayawati further clarified that, under the BSP's organisational policy, senior office-bearers and coordinators from Uttar Pradesh who are currently handling responsibilities in other states would not be assigned any organisational role in the state.
Article Summary: Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) president Mayawati on Sunday announced the expulsion of former Rajya Sabha member Ashok Siddarth from the party. Article Title: Delhi riots 2020: Why Tahir Hussain escaped death penalty in IB officer Ankit Sharma murder case
Article Text:
Why the court awarded life imprisonment instead of death

Prosecution sought death penalty

Defence argued case did not qualify as 'rarest of rare'

Court's conviction order

Murder during Delhi riots

NEW DELHI: A Delhi court on Friday sentenced former AAP councillor Tahir Hussain and four others to life imprisonment for the murder of Intelligence Bureau (IB) officer Ankit Sharma during the 2020 northeast Delhi riots, rejecting the prosecution's plea for the death penalty after holding that it had failed to prove the convicts were beyond the possibility of reformation.Additional Sessions Judge Praveen Singh pronounced the sentence after hearing arguments from both the prosecution and the defence on the quantum of punishment. The court said the prosecution had not established that the case met the threshold for awarding capital punishment, even though it had convicted Hussain and four others for Sharma's murder earlier this month.The judgment was delivered in the physical presence of Hussain and the other convicts amid tight security at Delhi's Karkardooma Court.While the Delhi Police had argued that the case fell within the "rarest of rare" category warranting capital punishment, the court concluded that the prosecution had not proved that the convicts were incapable of reform, a key principle laid down by the Supreme Court for awarding the death penalty.Additional Sessions Judge Praveen Singh observed that the prosecution was unable to establish that the convicts were beyond reformation, leading the court to impose life imprisonment instead.The prosecution had sought the death penalty for Hussain and the four co-convicts, arguing that the murder was brutal, deliberate and carried out without any provocation.During the sentencing hearing, Special Public Prosecutor Madhukar Pandey described the crime as "anti-social and abhorrent" and argued that it qualified as one of the "rarest of rare" cases.Pandey told the court that Sharma was subjected to a cold-blooded and savage attack with a heavy cutting weapon and that the killing could not be viewed in isolation because it occurred during the northeast Delhi riots in which 53 people lost their lives.According to the prosecution, Sharma sustained 51 injuries, seven of which were independently sufficient to cause death.The prosecution further submitted that the convicts acted without provocation and displayed complete disregard for the consequences of their actions.Earlier, Pandey had argued that the accused had fallen to the "level of being animals" while assaulting Sharma and said:"Those who are asking for mercy today should have shown mercy themselves. No mercy was shown from anyone's side. No one even took Ankit to the hospital. They are asking for mercy after committing such a brutal murder."The prosecution also argued that Hussain, being an elected municipal councillor at the time, had a greater responsibility to protect citizens instead of becoming part of the unlawful assembly.The defence, however, urged the court to show leniency, arguing that not every murder warranted capital punishment and that aggravating and mitigating circumstances must both be considered.Senior advocate Rajiv Mohan, appearing for Hussain, argued that six of the eleven accused in the case had already been acquitted and that the prosecution had failed to establish any conspiracy during the trial.The defence maintained that Hussain's conviction rested on his membership of an unlawful assembly and common intention rather than evidence showing he personally inflicted fatal injuries on Sharma.The counsel further argued that there had been no preparation or conspiracy, that Sharma had been attacked by a large crowd during widespread rioting and that Hussain's conduct during custody had remained satisfactory.Advocate Tara Narula also urged the court to consider Hussain's family circumstances, submitting that he had three children, an elderly father and that his wife was a homemaker dependent on rental income.Counsel representing the other convicts similarly pleaded for leniency, citing their family responsibilities and arguing that both communities had been involved in the violence.The court, however, rejected several of the defence's contentions before pronouncing the sentence.On July 13, the court convicted Hussain and four others for Sharma's murder.In its conviction order, the court held that Hussain was a member of a heavily armed mob that had assembled with animus against Hindus to commit rioting, arson and looting before murdering Sharma in what it described as a "savage and relentless assault."The court further held that the prosecution had proved members of the unlawful assembly knew that pursuing their common object could result in death.Ankit Sharma, an Intelligence Bureau officer, was killed during the northeast Delhi riots in February 2020 in the Dayalpur area. His mutilated body was later recovered from a drain.Hussain was convicted under Sections 302 (murder), 365 (kidnapping or abducting with intent secretly and wrongfully to confine a person), 147 (rioting), 148 (rioting armed with a deadly weapon), 153A (promoting enmity) and 188 (disobedience to an order duly promulgated by a public servant) of the Indian Penal Code, read with Section 149 relating to unlawful assembly.With Friday's sentencing order, Hussain and the four co-convicts will serve life imprisonment, while the court's decision underscores that despite the brutality of the crime, the legal threshold required for imposing the death penalty was not met because the prosecution failed to prove they were beyond the possibility of reformation.
Article Summary: A Delhi court sentenced former AAP councillor Tahir Hussain and four others to life imprisonment for the murder of Intelligence Bureau (IB) officer Ankit Sharma during the 2020 northeast Delhi riots. The court rejected the prosecution's plea for the death penalty after holding that it had failed to prove the convicts were beyond the possibility of reformation.

Article Title: Exiled Bangladeshi writer Taslima Nasreen returns to Kolkata after 19 years

NEW DELHI: AAP turncoat and BJP MP Raghav Chadha on Thursday broke his prolonged silence on the paper leak issue, speaking for the first time from the ruling side in Rajya Sabha. As BJP pushed the anti-paper leak Bill in the Parliament, Chadha said he did not want headlines but spoke "wholeheartedly in support of the students of India," adding that "PM Modi heard it just like the head of a family listens. "Chadha stressed that the paper leak crisis could only be resolved through an "institutional solution" and not through "media sound-bytes", which he claimed was the approach adopted by the PM Modi-led government.BJP leader said, "I don't want headline, but an outcome."Addressing NEET aspirants, he said, "Your anger is justified. Your pain is real. And your concerns about the examination system are genuine."He further said that when students raised their voices in protest, the Prime Minister listened and acted as a "guardian" to address their concerns."Students demanded, the government acted. Historic decisions taken. System changed," Chadha said.He also said that the government "heard and delivered."Highlighting the impact of paper leaks on students, he added, "Because a paper leak does not merely compromise an examination. It can wipe out years of preparation in a single moment."He further said, "Every student deserves an examination system where hard work and merit, not a leaked paper, decide the result."Months ago, Chadha led a rebel exodus from Arvind Kejriwal-founded AAP, with seven Rajya Sabha members from the party breaking away and merging their faction with the ruling BJP.However, the Bill came under sharp criticism from the Opposition in the Rajya Sabha. Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge led the attack after Union minister Jitendra Singh tabled the Bill in the Upper House.Parliament Thursday approved the Public Examination (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026, introducing stricter penalties for paper leaks and exam-related malpractices. The government said the legislation addresses one of the biggest concerns affecting students and called for cooperation from all stakeholders to tackle the issue.The Bill was passed by a voice vote in the Rajya Sabha amid an opposition walkout, a day after it cleared the Lok Sabha.Under the amended law, individuals found guilty of paper leaks or other unfair means in public examinations will face a minimum prison term of five years, extendable to 10 years, along with a fine of up to Rs 50 lakh.For organised exam-related crimes, the Bill prescribes a minimum jail term of seven years and a fine of up to Rs 10 crore.The legislation also empowers state governments and Union Territory administrations to designate Courts of Session as special fast-track courts to try offences under the Act. These courts will conduct day-to-day proceedings and complete trials within three months of the filing of the chargesheet.The Bill further authorises the central government to constitute a special task force to investigate offences under the Act whenever necessary.
Article Summary: BJP leader said, "I don't want headline, but an outcome" Chadha led a rebel exodus from Arvind Kejriwal-founded AAP, with seven Rajya Sabha members from the party breaking away and merging their faction with the ruling BJP.

KOLKATA/BURDWAN: West Bengal Police STF on Saturday arrested suspected terrorist Hamim Mondal's girlfriend, Arpita Sarkar, from Sahibganj in Jharkhand and said they are probing the duo's alleged plan to foment trouble at Jantar Mantar, the site of recent student protest.Hamim, who was allegedly tracking Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari, was arrested from a residential township in Burdwan Friday."Hamim was working under instructions received through social media and encrypted messaging apps from individuals using Pakistani handles and phone numbers. He was instructed to buy police uniforms and head to Jantar Mantar in Delhi with a group of men and women to create disturbance there. We are yet to ascertain whether he was able to build that team and travel to Delhi," said STF IG Gaurav Sharma.The STF tracked down Arpita while investigating Hamim's alleged links with Pakistan-based terror outfits. Cops said the two have known each other for four years, but she is not Hamim's only accomplice.They are investigating a recruitment network allegedly built by him over the past four to five months.Arpita was picked up after investigators found Instagram chats between her and Hamim.She was produced before a Burdwan court on Saturday and sent to STF custody for 13 days.She is also suspected of being involved in a honey-trap network that targeted influential people, including politicians. She was recently involved in honey-trapping the son of a senior Jharkhand minister, officers said.Investigators suspect Hamim was part of an ISI-backed module tasked with gathering intelligence on VIPs, including BJP functionaries, recruiting operatives and preparing the ground for possible terror activities in Bengal. He was allegedly recruited by Pakistan-based handlers around four-five months ago and tasked with bringing more men and women into the network. He roped in Arpita, among others."She helped Hamim develop contacts with influential political figures and collect their personal details. We are examining digital evidence and verifying the exact nature of her role," an STF officer said.Investigators said that Hamim and his Pakistan-based handlers communicated through WhatsApp, Telegram, Element X and Session.STF officers have identified four Pakistan-based handles - Abir Jat333, Uzair, Rana and Hamad - that were allegedly used to send instructions and assign tasks."It is suspected that these handles are linked to Pakistan's Shahzad Bhatti gang. "The investigation is still at a very nascent stage, and more persons are likely to be arrested in the coming days," he added.Police said while Hamim's ancestral home is in East Burdwan. His father lived in Howrah since 1998 for work.

Article Title: Ahead of Independence Day, police bust Pakistan-linked drone narco-arms racket; Rs 50 crore heroin seized
Article Text:
Police detained one accused, Virendra Singh, a resident of Jodhpur, who had allegedly arrived to receive the consignment.





JAISALMER: In a major breakthrough against cross-border smuggling ahead of Independence Day, Rajasthan Police on Sunday foiled an alleged Pakistan-backed drone-based narco-arms smuggling attempt in Bikaner's Khajuwala sector, seizing 10 kg of "999 Marka" Afghan heroin valued at around Rs 50 crore, along with 11 sophisticated foreign-made pistols, 22 magazines and 100 live rounds of ammunition.The operation, codenamed Operation SHOCKWAVE, was conducted under the supervision of Bikaner Superintendent of Police Mridul Kachhawa and is being regarded as one of the biggest recent successes against an international drone-based narcotics and arms smuggling network operating along the India-Pakistan border.Based on specific Human Intelligence (HUMINT) inputs and technical surveillance, police intercepted suspected smugglers after they collected a consignment allegedly dropped by a drone from across the Pakistan border in an agricultural field in the 6 BD area under Khajuwala police station limits. The accused were intercepted while transporting the consignment on a motorcycle.Police detained one accused, Virendra Singh, a resident of Jodhpur, who had allegedly arrived to receive the consignment. The remaining accused have been identified and named, and efforts are underway to arrest them. Preliminary investigation has revealed links between the cross-border narco-arms syndicate and operatives in Punjab.SP Mridul Kachhawa said the gang had been under police surveillance for a considerable period. Continuous intelligence inputs, technical monitoring and field verification enabled investigators to execute the operation successfully and prevent the contraband from reaching criminal networks.The seized consignment included 10 kg of 99.9 per cent pure "999 Marka" Afghan heroin bearing the Helmand mark, along with an arsenal of sophisticated firearms comprising two Turkey-made Zigana pistols, four Glock pistols, five Star-marked Chinese pistols, 22 magazines and 100 live cartridges.Officials said the operation underlined the growing threat posed by Pakistan-based drone smuggling networks attempting to push narcotics and weapons across the international border.With Independence Day approaching, security agencies have been placed on high alert and surveillance along the border has been intensified to prevent any infiltration or smuggling attempts.The operation was supported by the Bikaner Police Cyber Cell, with Deepak Yadav, head constable Vasudev charan and Shriram playing a key role in technical analysis and intelligence gathering.Police have seized the entire consignment and launched a detailed investigation to identify the complete network behind the operation. Investigators are examining the syndicate's links with Pakistan and tracing its connections to other Indian states.Officials said further arrests are expected as the probe progresses.
Article Summary: Rajasthan Police on Sunday foiled an alleged Pakistan-backed drone-based narco- arms smuggling attempt. Police seized 10 kg of "999 Marka" Afghan heroin valued at around Rs 50 crore, along with 11 sophisticated foreign-made pistols, 22 magazines and 100 live rounds of ammunition.

Article Title: BSF joins Rajasthan forest department to protect endangered caracal along India-Pakistan border
Article Text: JAISALMER: The Border Security Force (BSF), which guards India's international borders, will now play a significant role in the conservation of the highly endangered Schedule I wild animal, the Caracal, in the border areas of Jaisalmer in collaboration with the Rajasthan Forest Department.The joint initiative aims to create a favourable environment for the conservation of the elusive desert cat, strengthen the participation of local communities, and safeguard the unique biodiversity of the Thar Desert.A high-level team comprising Director of the Wildlife Institute of India, Dr. Govind Sagar Bhardwaj, Divisional Chief Conservator of Forests, Jodhpur, Anup K.R., Deputy Conservator of Forests (IGNP Stage-II, Jaisalmer) Devendra Singh Bhati, and Assistant Conservator of Forests Ranjeet Singh Dholia visited the border villages and Border Out Posts (BOPs) at Dhanana, Murar, Navtala, Ghotaru and Moomal along the India-Pakistan International Border.During the visit, the officials conducted a field assessment of potential and historical Caracal habitats, examined ecologically important sites, and held discussions with BSF officers and personnel on future conservation strategies.Deputy Conservator of Forests Devendra Singh Bhati said that the Forest Department and the BSF are jointly working to create a conducive environment for Caracal conservation in the border region while encouraging greater participation of local communities in protecting the species and preserving the fragile desert ecosystem.Officers and personnel of the BSF stationed at Murar and Moomal Border Out Posts expressed their commitment to supporting conservation efforts. The BSF assured the Forest Department that it would assist in collecting information on Caracal sightings and strengthen coordination for monitoring and conservation activities in the border areas.As part of the awareness campaign, BSF will display Caracal conservation posters at all Border Out Posts near Tanot, Babooliyan, Longewala, Kishangarh and Ghotaru to educate troops and local residents about the importance of protecting the species.During the field visit, scientists from the Wildlife Institute of India, including Sashirth Vatsal and his team, conducted an extensive survey of the border landscape, natural habitats and biodiversity-rich sites, and discussed long-term conservation strategies for the Caracal.The primary objective of the visit was to assess the species' historical and potential habitats and to prioritise the conservation of the Caracal—also known locally as Syahgosh—one of the rarest and most elusive predators of the Thar Desert. Officials emphasised that the Caracal is an important predator in the desert ecosystem and serves as an indicator of a healthy and balanced biodiversity. They stressed that habitat protection, human-wildlife coexistence and continuous monitoring are essential for its long-term survival.Bhati said the team also interacted with local residents and highlighted the importance of community participation in conserving the rare species. He noted that sustained awareness campaigns and local support would play a decisive role in ensuring the Caracal's survival in the region.Officials further pointed out that the border desert ecosystem also supports several important bird species, including the Sindh Sparrow, Roller, Steppe Eagle and various vulture species. The Forest Department is simultaneously focusing on protecting these birds and their habitats to maintain the ecological balance and long-term sustainability of the Thar Desert.
Article Summary: The Caracal is one of the rarest and most elusive predators of the Thar Desert. The initiative aims to create a favourable environment for the conservation of the elusive desert cat. It also aims to strengthen the participation of local communities in protecting the species.

Article Title: What is CJP's next move? Core members to meet in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar on Aug 5 to chart future course

CHHATRAPATI SAMBHAJINAGAR: Core members of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) will meet at founder Abhijeet Dipke's residence in Maharashtra's Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar on August 5 to discuss the outfit's future course of action, sources said on Sunday.According to news agency PTI, CJP activists and volunteers were asked to spend time with their families after the outfit's month-long agitation against the alleged NEET paper leak at Delhi's Jantar Mantar last month.The core members of the CJP were also asked to interact with volunteers and students and bring their feedback, views and suggestions to the upcoming meeting, sources said.The outfit will hold a press conference after the August 5 meeting to announce decisions on its future course of action, sources said.Meanwhile, Dipke met students, locals and visitors from neighbouring districts at his residence and celebrated Friendship Day with children.Earlier, Abhijeet Dipke urged Prime Minister Narendra Modi to go beyond social media gestures and direct authorities to withdraw cases filed against student protesters."Don't just offer forgiveness on Instagram; direct the police to withdraw the cases as well. Withdraw the cases filed against these students," Dipke told ANI.Demanding a formal apology over the police action against students on July 20, Dipke said the Prime Minister's "forgiveness" could not be discussed unless the government first acknowledged the alleged "brutality" faced by the protesters."PM Modi should apologise to the students who were subjected to a lathicharge on July 20, those who suffered head injuries, pellet gun wounds, and serious injuries such as broken arms and legs. Apologise to them first; only then can you talk about forgiveness," he said.The CJP-led protests at Delhi's Jantar Mantar over the alleged NEET paper leak scandal received widespread support from Gen Z across the country, eventually leading to Union Education minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation last week.

I was personally abused, and even my late mother was subjected to abuse. He urged people to forgive them, guide them in the right direction, and help them reform, saying the students had "lost their way" but deserved an opportunity to correct themselves.The Prime Minister further argued against prolonged legal action and social ostracisation."Punishing them, dragging them through court proceedings, and harassing them in society, none of this will change the situation. Earlier on Thursday, after PM Modi released a video message highlighting the recently passed anti-paper leak legislation, Dipke commented on Instagram, "Your skin is brighter than the country's future."The Prime Minister had described the legislation as a key reform aimed at strengthening the examination system.

Article Title: Bhiwandi crash: Buiding owner, repairs contractor booked; state orders probe
Article Text:
A five-storey Bhiwandi building collapsed, killing ten people and injuring three others

Hundreds of dangerous buildings in MMR, thousands at risk (Photo credit: Santosh Gupta)





MUMBAI: The state govt ordered an inquiry into the crash of a part of a five-storey Bhiwandi building that claimed 10 lives.An FIR was lodged against the contractor hired for repairs, Ashok, and building owner, Bilal Khan, under Sections 105 (culpable homicide not amounting to murder) and 125 (negligent act endangering human life or personal safety of others) of BNS and relevant provisions of Maharashtra Regional and Town Planning Act for illegal construction, said DCP (zone 2), Thane, Pawan Basod.The PM announced an ex gratia of Rs 2 lakh each for the families of those killed and the CM Rs 5 lakh each.This was the third such major building collapse in Bhiwandi since 2020.Repairs began four days earlier after residents flagged falling plaster chunks and hired a contractor on their own. The building was not vacated during the work.Around 8pm on Thursday, residents noticed that a supporting pillar in wing B had developed a crack and was tilting, alerted the contractor and vacated the building.Workers were immediately brought in and the pillar was reinforced with iron support rods. Assuming that the structure had been stabilised, many residents went back into the building around 11.30pm.Moments later, half the wing collapsed, trapping many residents and labourers under the rubble.Over the next 15 hours, NDRF, fire brigade and Thane disaster response force personnel pulled out the bodies of Rakesh Paswan (25), Mukesh Paswan (30), Ashok Paswan (40), Krish Kumar (32), Ranjit Singh (45), Radheshyam Kushwaha (45), Siraj Rasul Sheikh (45), Shamim Ansari (32), Shyam Pal (40), and Santosh Pandey (42).Those injured, Abhay Yadav (26), Deepak Yadav (25) and Sangeeta Prajapati (36), were taken to a hospital. Some residents were rescued from the portion of the wing that remained standing.An NDRF officer said the building suffered a “pancake collapse”, in which one floor falls directly onto another.“The chances of survival in such collapses are extremely low. We deployed trained sniffer dogs to locate the victims.”Disaster management minister Girish Mahajan, who visited the site, said the repairs were carried out late at night to escape civic scrutiny.He directed the authorities to ensure that all dangerous buildings in Bhiwandi are vacated and appropriate action.Mehtab Ansari, a resident, told TOI that all flat owners had contributed around Rs 10,000 each for the repairs.Another resident, Komal Arvind Gupta, alleged that negligence during the work damaged the pillar.
Article Summary: An FIR was lodged against the contractor hired for repairs, Ashok, and building owner, Bilal Khan, under Sections 105 (culpable homicide not amounting to murder) and 125 (negligent act endangering human life or personal safety of others) The PM announced an ex gratia of Rs 2 lakh each for the families of those killed.

Article Title: Spain says most migrants return to Morocco after border rush kills 57
Article Text:
As thousands gathered near the border, Moroccan security forces used batons and tear gas to push back crowds

Spain said on Friday that it had regained control of a massive migrant surge into its North African enclave of Ceuta, with most of the more than 50,000 people who crossed the border by land and sea voluntarily returning to Morocco. The unprecedented influx left dozens dead and triggered political tensions across Europe.Spanish authorities said 57 bodies had been recovered on the Spanish side of the border. Officials warned that the death toll could be higher as there may have been additional casualties on the Moroccan side. According to the government, some migrants drowned while others were crushed as they attempted to climb the breakwater supporting the border fence.Spain's interior ministry said around 50,000 migrants entered Ceuta between Thursday and Friday, with about 48,300 having already returned to Morocco by Friday evening. Ceuta regional president Juan Jesus Vivas, however, estimated that the total number of crossings could have reached 60,000 over the two days.As thousands gathered near the border, Moroccan security forces used batons and tear gas to push back crowds and prevent more people from entering the Spanish territory.Reuters reporters at the scene also saw riot police firing tear gas, while water cannon vehicles were deployed to disperse migrants. Burnt remains of a bus and seven cars were visible following clashes.On the Spanish side, military vehicles were positioned along sections of the border as hundreds of migrants remained stranded on the Moroccan side. Several hundred people later crossed back through official checkpoints and openings in the fence, with many saying they were unable to find food or shelter in Ceuta. "I'm going back," one migrant told news agency Reuters.Spanish prime minister Pedro Sanchez travelled to Ceuta on Friday, where he faced protests and jeers from demonstrators. He described the mass border crossing as "a violation of Spain's territorial sovereignty" and said authorities were accelerating the return of those who had entered illegally with Morocco's full cooperation.The incident also exposed divisions within Europe over migration policy. Italy announced it was temporarily suspending the European Union's Schengen border-free travel arrangements with Spain, a decision that would affect air and sea travel between the two countries. Madrid criticised the move, saying it breached European Union treaties.Ceuta and Melilla, Spain's two autonomous enclaves in North Africa, form the European Union's only land borders with Africa. While both regularly witness attempts by migrants to enter Europe, Spanish authorities described the latest influx as unprecedented.Several right-wing political parties across Europe blamed the crisis on Spain's migration policies, including this year's amnesty for hundreds of thousands of undocumented migrants. Spain also summoned the Italian ambassador after Italian Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani claimed the amnesty had "encouraged human trafficking".US President Donald Trump also weighed in on the crisis, describing the situation at Ceuta as an invasion.The crossings "look like an invasion", Trump said, adding, "That same thing's going to happen to us if the Republicans don't get elected, except worse," referring to the upcoming US midterm elections.The US state department also criticised Spain's handling of migration, saying the incident was "the direct result of the Spanish Government's deliberate efforts to enable and facilitate mass illegal migration into Europe." It added, "We are considering actions to defend Americans at home and abroad from this threat and stand ready to assist other European allies considering similar option."Meanwhile, France said it would significantly strengthen security along its border with Spain.French interior minister Laurent Nunez announced that the police presence would be increased fivefold by Saturday, alongside enhanced aerial surveillance and additional patrols on trains.Spain's Guardia Civil police association AUGC also criticised the handling of the situation, saying there had been too few officers deployed at the border fence during the surge, leaving security forces unable to stop the mass crossings.
Article Summary: Spain says it has regained control of a massive migrant surge into its North African enclave of Ceuta. Most of the more than 50,000 people who crossed the border by land and sea voluntarily returned to Morocco. The unprecedented influx left dozens dead and triggered political tensions across Europe.

Article Title: 4.7-magnitude earthquake hits Italy; buildings damaged, four injured
Article Text:
4.7-magnitude earthquake strikes Italy, injures four (Reuters image)

A 4.7-magnitude earthquake struck the volcanic Campi Flegrei (Phlegraean Fields) area near the southern Italian city of Naples on Friday, injuring four people, damaging buildings and churches. It also triggered power outages that disrupted train and metro services.The earthquake struck at 7.46 pm (local time), with its epicentre in the Campi Flegrei volcanic area west of Naples at a depth of about 3 km (2 miles), according to Italy's National Institute of Geophysics and Volcanology.The Italian fire service said minor damage was reported to buildings in and around Naples, but added that emergency crews had not received any immediate requests for rescue or assistance, as cited by Reuters.As a precaution, local authorities suspended rail and metro services while inspections were carried out.Italian media described the tremor as one of the strongest ever recorded in the Campi Flegrei area, prompting residents in several neighbourhoods to rush onto the streets as the ground shook.Campi Flegrei, a densely populated volcanic caldera that spans much of western Naples, has witnessed increasingly frequent seismic activity in recent years, prompting Italian authorities to intensify monitoring of the area.While low-intensity tremors are common in the region, stronger earthquakes have revived concerns over a repeat of the seismic crisis of the early 1980s, which caused widespread disruption and forced thousands of residents to evacuate their homes.Italy is prone to earthquakes due to its geological setting. In 2016, a series of powerful quakes struck central Italy, devastating parts of the Lazio, Umbria and Marche regions and killing around 300 people.The country's deadliest earthquake in recent decades was the 6.9-magnitude Irpinia quake in southern Italy in November 1980, which claimed about 2,700 lives and devastated hundreds of towns.
Article Summary: 4.7-magnitude earthquake strikes Italy, injures four people. Epicentre in Campi Flegrei volcanic area west of Naples at a depth of about 3 km. Italian media described tremor as one of the strongest ever recorded.

Article Title: US Marine F-35 fighter jet crashes in San Diego, pilot ejects safely
Article Text:
Military officials said the cause of the crash is being investigated.

A US Marine Corps F-35 fighter jet crashed near Marine Corps Air Station (MCAS) Miramar in San Diego on Friday, with the pilot ejecting safely before the aircraft burst into flames and sparked a brush fire, military officials said.The fighter aircraft, attached to the 3rd Marine Aircraft Wing and Marine Aircraft Group 11, went down at around 10 am local time near the air station. The Marine Corps described the incident as an "aircraft mishap".First Lieutenant Blake Starbuck told Fox News that the crash was a "Class A mishap involving a Marine Corps F-35B in the vicinity of MCAS Miramar".Lieutenant Starbuck confirmed that the pilot successfully ejected and was safely recovered after the aircraft came down. Military officials said the cause of the crash is being investigated.Starbuck said he could not immediately confirm the purpose of the flight, including whether the aircraft had been taking off, landing or carrying out a training mission.He also said there was no immediate information about any injuries or fatalities linked to the crash.Television footage from SkyRanger 7 showed the wreckage split into two large sections in the middle of a burnt field roughly the size of a football pitch.Large flames and thick black smoke rose from the crash site, which was located north of State Route 52, making the fire visible to motorists on the nearby highway. The San Diego Fire-Rescue Department said it had joined efforts to contain the brush fire triggered by the crash.However, officials said the military remains in charge of the crash site and will lead the investigation into the incident.
Article Summary: US Marine Corps F-35 fighter jet crashed near Marine Corps Air Station (MCAS) Miramar in San Diego on Friday. Pilot ejected safely before the aircraft burst into flames and sparked a brush fire. Military officials said the cause of the crash is being investigated.

Article Title: This 44-year-old Swedish man survived being buried beneath a metre of snow for nearly two months against all odds
Article Text:
Image: Left/The Telegraph/Right/The Guardian

Snowmobilers uncovered the buried car after noticing something unusual beneath the snow

Doctors believed melted snow and an extremely slow metabolism helped keep him alive

The case challenged assumptions about the limits of human survival

One of the most remarkable modern survival stories

In December 2011, a 44-year-old Swedish man named Peter Skyllberg disappeared while driving through the country's frozen north. Weeks passed with no sign of him as winter temperatures plunged well below freezing. Then, in February 2012, a group of snowmobilers spotted what looked like the roof of a car protruding from a snowdrift. Digging through nearly a metre of snow, they made an astonishing discovery: inside sat the missing driver, alive but severely weakened after spending almost two months trapped inside the snow-covered vehicle with little or no food. His extraordinary survival stunned doctors and scientists alike, raising questions about how the human body can endure prolonged starvation and extreme cold under exceptional circumstances. The case remains one of the most remarkable survival stories on record, highlighting the body's extraordinary ability to adapt under rare conditions while continuing to inform medical understanding of hypothermia, starvation and human resilience.Peter Skyllberg, a 44-year-old Swedish man, had apparently become stranded on a remote road after his vehicle was immobilised by heavy snowfall during late December.As reported by the BBC, over the following weeks, repeated snowstorms gradually buried the car beneath roughly one metre of snow, leaving only a small portion visible above the surface. On 17 February 2012, passing snowmobilers noticed the unusual shape beneath the snow and stopped to investigate. After digging into the drift, they found the driver sitting inside the vehicle, barely able to move or speak but still conscious. Emergency responders transported him by helicopter to hospital, where doctors began treating him for severe dehydration, malnutrition and hypothermia.Medical specialists estimated that the man had survived for close to two months with virtually no food. According to doctors treating him, he is believed to have survived primarily by melting and drinking snow, preventing fatal dehydration while his body relied on stored fat reserves for energy. Physicians also suggested that prolonged exposure to cold may have pushed his body into an extreme energy-conservation state, dramatically slowing metabolism and reducing calorie requirements.Rather than freezing, the man may have benefited from the very snow that trapped him. The thick blanket of snow covering the vehicle acted as a natural insulating layer, shielding the interior from the harshest outdoor temperatures and helping maintain a more stable environment than the open air outside.Although humans can survive for weeks without food under certain conditions, surviving for nearly two months in such an isolated environment is exceptionally rare.Doctors involved in the case described the survival as extraordinary, noting that each situation depends on numerous factors, including hydration, body fat, physical activity, environmental conditions and underlying health.The Swedish case also highlighted the protective role snow can sometimes play. While heavy snowfall often creates life-threatening situations, deep snow can also trap pockets of relatively warmer air, reducing heat loss in much the same way that insulated shelters or snow caves protect mountaineers during winter storms.The man's identity was never widely publicised, and after receiving medical treatment he gradually recovered from the ordeal.His case remains one of the most extraordinary documented examples of human endurance in modern times. Rather than surviving through extraordinary supplies or specialised equipment, he endured weeks of isolation using little more than melted snow while remaining inside a vehicle buried beneath winter drifts.The incident continues to fascinate survival experts and physicians because it demonstrates how, under exceptional circumstances, the human body can adapt far beyond what most people would consider possible. It also serves as a reminder of both the dangers of remote winter travel and the remarkable resilience that can emerge when survival depends on conserving every possible ounce of energy.
Article Summary: Peter Skyllberg, a 44-year-old Swedish man, had apparently become stranded on a remote road after his vehicle was immobilised by heavy snowfall. Snowmobilers uncovered the buried car after noticing something unusual beneath the snow. Doctors believed melted snow and an extremely slow metabolism helped keep him alive. The case challenged assumptions about the limits of human survival.

Article Title: Days after Trump's dismissal, report claims Russia shared military intelligence with Iran
Article Text: Days after US President Donald Trump downplayed Russia's alleged support to Iran, saying any assistance from Moscow had been "very unimpactful", a report claiming Russia is providing Tehran with intel to strengthen its military capabilities has surfaced. This comes amid the ongoing conflict with the United States.Citing US and European officials familiar with the matter, NBC News reported that Russia has been supplying Iran with electronic intelligence, including satellite surveillance and signals intelligence. The report further said the intelligence could help improve Tehran's air defences, enhance the precision of its drone and missile strikes, and better track US military movements during aerial operations.Neither Russia nor Iran has publicly commented on the report, and the claims have not been independently verified.The report surfaced days after Trump dismissed Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy's allegations that Russia was actively assisting Iran.Speaking to reporters aboard Air Force One on July 28, before his meetings at the White House with Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu and later with Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy, Trump said he would personally seek clarification from Russian president Vladimir Putin."We'll find out if that's true. I'll ask Putin about it. We'll find out," Trump said.Trump argued that any Russian assistance had failed to alter the battlefield."It hasn't had much impact because we've knocked the hell out of it (Iran)...They may be providing support, but if they are, it hasn't worked out because they (Iran) have no army, they have no air force, they have no navy, they have nothing," he remarked.Drawing a comparison with Venezuela's military equipment, Trump added, "They (Russia) gave Venezuela a lot of equipment. Venezuela had all Russian equipment. How did that work? Not too good.""I don't think they've been doing it, certainly not at a high level. And if they have, it has been very unimpactful," Trump said.Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has repeatedly accused Russia of providing Iran with satellite intelligence. He has claimed that Ukrainian intelligence found Moscow was conducting satellite surveillance of US military facilities and critical infrastructure in the Gulf before sharing the information with Tehran."I will instruct our intelligence to share with our partners the information we have regarding Russia's new assistance to the Iranian regime," Zelenskyy said, before him meeting with Trump.In a post on X, the Ukrainian president wrote, "Since the beginning of July, we have recorded active Russian satellite surveillance of the Gulf states and U.S. military facilities located there. These images subsequently appear in Iran."The latest claims come against the backdrop of rapidly expanding ties between Moscow and Tehran. In January, Russia and Iran signed a comprehensive strategic partnership agreement covering defence, trade, energy and security cooperation, though it stopped short of creating a formal mutual defence pact.Military cooperation between the two countries has also deepened since the outbreak of the Ukraine war. Western governments have repeatedly accused Iran of supplying drones and other military equipment to Russia for use in Ukraine, allegations that both Moscow and Tehran have denied.Russia has also publicly backed Iran following recent US and Israeli strikes targeting Iranian military and nuclear facilities.
Article Summary: NBC News reports that Russia has been supplying Iran with electronic intelligence, including satellite surveillance and signals intelligence. This comes days after US President Donald Trump downplayed Russia's alleged support to Iran, saying any assistance from Moscow had been "very unimpactful"

Article Title: Despite Trump's backing, Vivek Ramaswamy can't curry favor with MAGA bros in Ohio
Article Text:
Vivek Ramaswamy finds himself in a surprisingly competitive contest against Democrat Amy Acton

The TOI correspondent from Washington

: Every Indian child grows up hearing at least two pieces of parental advice: study hard, and don't talk back. Vivek Ramaswamy followed the first well enough to become a biotech billionaire before he turned forty. But talking down at a tetchy MAGA townhall on Friday appears to have thrown his campaign for Ohio governor into turmoil.The Cincinnati-born Indian-American Republican candidate lasted barely 14 minutes into a speech before exiting from a Young Americans for Liberty conference after a section of the audience turned hostile. The moment that appeared to sink the evening came when Ramaswamy, attempting a generational appeal, declared: "The truth of the matter is, people in my generation have already made it. We're gonna be fine. It's going to be your generation that pays the price. " Boos and jeers followed the comment, one heckler branding him a "political cretin," and asking him to "get the f-outta here," as the biotech bro eased away with an ironic "Peace out."The episode lands at a delicate moment in Ramaswamy's gubernatorial campaign. Once seen as the overwhelming favourite after securing MAGA boss Donald Trump's endorsement and sweeping the Republican primary, he now finds himself in a surprisingly competitive contest against Democrat Amy Acton in a state that has become reliably Republican over the past decade.Recent polling suggests a race that is effectively tied, a startling development in a state Trump won comfortably.Trump's endorsement remains one of Ramaswamy's biggest political assets. The President backed him early, and Ohio Republicans dutifully rallied behind him, giving him institutional support rarely seen so far ahead of an election. But as Trump's own approval ratings have sagged amid the Iran conflict, weighed down by persistent inflation and affordability concerns, Republicans in mid-term races are increasingly discovering that presidential coattails can sometimes resemble ankle weights.This appears to have led to a subtle recalibration in Ramaswamy's messaging. Whereas he once enthusiastically echoed Trump's "MAGA" slogan, he has lately preferred variations such as making "America and Ohio greater than we have ever been," emphasizing future growth over nostalgic restoration in an attempt to create daylight between himself and Trump without actually stepping out of the presidential shadow.If elected, Ramaswamy would make history as America's third governor of Indian origin after Bobby Jindal in Louisiana and Nikki Haley in South Carolina -- and its first Hindu-American governor. Unlike some earlier Indian-American politicians who downplayed their religious identity, Ramaswamy has worn his Hindu faith openly, frequently discussing it on the campaign trail.Ironically, that openness has also made him a lightning rod for the MAGA fringe. White nationalist commentator Nick Fuentes has become one of his fiercest critics, arguing that Ramaswamy, as the American-born son of Indian immigrants, has no business lecturing "heritage Americans." Fuentes has gone so far as to urge conservatives to vote for Democrat Acton rather than allow Ramaswamy to become governor, accusing him of dismissing concerns over immigration and demographic change.Ramaswamy's personal fortune has generated another line of attack. Worth hundreds of millions of dollars after founding biotech company Roivant Sciences and building wealth through financial investments, he has been portrayed by critics as another patronizing billionaire offering pious lectures on economic hardship. His remark that his own generation had "already made it" inadvertently reinforced the caricature his opponents have tried to paint -- a wealthy entrepreneur struggling to sound relatable to anxious young voters.Ohio may yet send him to the governor's mansion, but Friday’s boos and jeers served as an unmistakable reminder that in contemporary American politics, loyalty is prized, celebrity helps, money certainly doesn't hurt. But no politician, however polished, is ever more than one ill-timed sentence away from discovering that even home audiences can turn on a quote.

The moment that appeared to sink the evening came when Ramaswamy, attempting a generational appeal, declared: "The truth of the matter is, people in my generation have already made it"

Article Title: How Iraqi engineer Azzam Alwash left California to restore Iraq's ancient marshes after decades of destruction
Article Text:
2013 Goldman Environmental Prize-winning engineer Azzam Alwash. Image credits: @goldmanprize/Instagram

Why Saddam Hussein deliberately drained the marshes

How Alwash's own history connected him to the marshes

What it took to actually bring water back to the marshes

How much of the marshes have actually recovered

Why the marshes' recovery remains fragile

In 2003, Azzam Alwash, an Iraqi-born civil engineer who had spent decades building a comfortable life in California, left his wife and two daughters in Los Angeles and returned to a country still in the middle of war, determined to undo one of the most deliberate environmental disasters of the late twentieth century. In the 1990s, Saddam Hussein had ordered the systematic draining of the vast Mesopotamian marshes in southern Iraq , destroying roughly 90 per cent of a wetland ecosystem widely believed to be among the sites associated with the biblical Garden of Eden, as punishment for the region's role in a Shiite uprising against his regime. More than two decades after Alwash arrived to begin reflooding the land, somewhere between 40 and 60 per cent of the original marshes have returned, according to conservation groups that have tracked the restoration. Before Alwash ever arrived with formal engineering plans, local Marsh Arabs had already started reclaiming their homeland themselves, quietly proving that restoration sometimes begins with ordinary people refusing to accept destruction as permanent.The Mesopotamian marshes, formed where the Tigris and Euphrates rivers converge in southern Iraq, had supported human communities for thousands of years before their destruction.According to the Goldman Environmental Prize, which later honoured Alwash for his restoration work, Saddam Hussein's regime burned, drained and poisoned the marshes in the mid-1990s, specifically in retaliation against Shiite Muslims who had staged an uprising following the Gulf War and fled into the marshes for refuge. The area's Indigenous population, known as the Marsh Arabs or Madan, had lived there in reed houses for centuries, relying on fishing, water buffalo herding and reed harvesting largely unchanged for generations.According to testimony Alwash gave before a US congressional subcommittee in 2004, preserved in State Department archival records , as many as 300,000 marsh dwellers died or were displaced during this period, as Saddam's forces drained the wetlands specifically to allow tanks and military vehicles access to root out rebel fighters hiding within the reeds.Alwash was born in Kut, Iraq, in 1958, and spent much of his childhood in Nasiriyah, on the fringes of the southern marshes, paddling through the reeds with his father, who worked as a district irrigation engineer for Iraq's Water Ministry. He moved to California in 1978, where he trained as a civil engineer, married and started a family, building a life far removed from the country of his birth. Through the 1990s, according to the Goldman Environmental Prize, Alwash watched from the United States as Saddam's regime dammed, drained and destroyed the marshes he remembered from childhood, and founded a nonprofit with his then-wife specifically to advocate for their conservation, even before he was able to return to Iraq himself.Everything else in the piece stays the same. This also matches the State Department archival record I cited later in the piece, which independently describes him as "a native of Al-Kut," so the correction brings the two sourced facts into alignment rather than leaving them in tension.Once on the ground, Alwash found that Marsh Arabs had already begun taking matters into their own hands, puncturing holes in the dams and levees that Saddam's government had built to keep the marshes dry. Alwash went on to found the nonprofit Nature Iraq to formalise and expand this restoration effort, leading a team of scientists and engineers working to systematically reflood the drained wetlands.According to UNEP, the United Nations Environment Programme has itself been working with local partners since 2004 to support the marshes' restoration, helping coordinate international support through related environmental agreements including the Ramsar Convention on wetlands and the Convention on Biological Diversity, working alongside Iraqi government ministries to rebuild the governance structures needed to manage the recovering ecosystem long term.According to Wetlands International, by 2000 roughly 90 per cent of the marshes had been destroyed through large-scale drainage under Saddam's regime, and following the fall of that regime, somewhere between 40 and 60 per cent of the original marshland extent was reflooded. Separate figures compiled through UNESCO 's own World Heritage documentation put current recovery at closer to 60 to 70 per cent of the marshes' historic extent, reflecting the difficulty of measuring recovery precisely across such a large and ecologically dynamic wetland system.In 2016, this partial but substantial recovery culminated in the Ahwar of Southern Iraq being formally inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List, recognising both the site's natural biodiversity and its connection to the ancient Sumerian cities of Ur, Uruk and Eridu, which sit along the marshes' historic edges.Despite this progress, conservation groups have consistently cautioned that the marshes' partial recovery remains vulnerable. According to Wetlands International, the reflooded wetlands continue to face serious pressure from large dam construction and expanding agricultural water use further upstream in Turkey, Iraq and Iran, both of which significantly reduce the volume of water reaching the marshes each year. Iraq's Mesopotamian Marshlands National Park, established on paper in 2013, has struggled to translate that formal designation into consistent on-the-ground management and protection.More than two decades after Alwash first returned to a war zone to begin this work, the Mesopotamian marshes stand as a rare example of large scale, community driven wetland restoration carried out under some of the most difficult political and security conditions imaginable, a recovery that remains genuinely underway rather than complete, still shaped as much by upstream water politics today as by the deliberate destruction that first drove Alwash back to the country he had left behind.
