Article Title: 'Extensive response plans': Iran threatens US energy sites after Trump warning
Article Text:
The official warned that Tehran had prepared "extensive response plans"

Iran has warned it is prepared to retaliate against any fresh US or Israeli attacks by targeting critical energy infrastructure across the region, hours after the White House signalled that President Donald Trump was considering expanding military operations against Tehran.According to Iran's state-affiliated Tasnim News Agency, a senior security official dismissed reports of possible US and Israeli strikes on Iranian infrastructure as "a kind of madness". The official warned that Tehran had prepared "extensive response plans", including strikes on Israeli critical infrastructure and US energy infrastructure across the region. The report added that Iran's armed forces have both "the capability and the will" to carry out such attacks.The warning came after White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt accused Iran of violating last month's truce agreement and escalating hostilities. "President Trump is not going to stand by and allow this terrorist behavior to occur," Leavitt said. "Iran will continue to pay until they come to the table in, what President Trump deems, a meaningful way."Earlier on Friday, Trump indicated that further US military action remained on the table, telling reporters at Camp David: "We just want to win" in Iran.He added, "We'll be hitting them very hard. You know, at some point they're going to say, 'We just can't take it anymore.'"The exchange followed another day of rising tensions in the Gulf. Iran's Revolutionary Guard claimed it had struck two oil tankers attempting to transit the Strait of Hormuz, a vital route for global energy supplies. Iranian state media also reported that four other tankers had turned back.Meanwhile, Kuwait said it intercepted Iranian drones that entered its airspace and were targeting military facilities hosting US forces. The country's defence ministry reported material damage caused by falling debris but said there were no casualties.
Article Summary: Senior security official dismissed reports of possible US and Israeli strikes on Iranian infrastructure as "a kind of madness" The official warned that Tehran had prepared "extensive response plans", including strikes on Israeli critical infrastructure and US energy infrastructure. The warning came after White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt accused Iran of violating last month's truce agreement.

Article Title: Delhi Mosque Demolition: Delhi Demolition Drive Near Faiz-e-Elahi Mosque: Police Clash During MCD Action
Article Text:
Delhi demolition drive: MCD carries out action near Faiz-e-Elahi mosque following HC order; 5 cops injured in stone pelting

Delhi: 5 Cops Injured, 10 Detained As Anti-Encroachment Drive Near Mosque Turns Violent

Demolition drive at Faiz-e-Ilahi Mosque near Turkman Gate in Delhi on Wednesday. Image Credit: Tarun Rawat/TNN







NEW DELHI: Multiple police personnel were injured during a demolition drive in central Delhi early on Wednesday after locals and miscreants attacked them with stones.The police is trying to identify the miscreants who engaged in stone-pelting and will initiate strict action against them.Delhi Police have registered an FIR against unknown persons and around 10 people have been detained for questioning so far, officials said.Police are scanning CCTV footage, ground visuals and body-camera recordings to identify those involved in the attack on the police team.While the FIR has been lodged against unidentified persons, investigators said four to five suspects have already been identified and further legal action will follow.Special commissioner (Law and Order) Ravindra Yadav said that the action started around 1 am."MCD conducted demolition as per the high court's orders on the encroached land. Stones were pelted at the police at night. We used minimal force to push back."DCP (Central) Nidhin Valsan said, "The action is still ongoing. We deployed our staff for security. 4 to 5 officers suffered minor injuries. As soon as we get the CCTV camera footage, ground footage, and body camera footage, we will identify the miscreants and take legal action."The demolition was carried out by the MCD to remove illegal constructions around the Faiz-e-Ilahi Mosque in the Turkman Gate area. The drive kicked off around 1 am, with around 17 bulldozers pressed into service.The action followed an order of the Delhi High Court, which declared a dispensary and a community hall adjoining the mosque illegal and directed their removal.The administration appealed to local residents to maintain peace.Anticipating major disruptions, the Delhi Traffic Police also issued a traffic advisory, warning of congestion on several key roads on Wednesday. Traffic around Ramlila Maidan and adjoining areas is expected to remain affected through the day.
Article Summary: 5 cops injured in stone pelting during demolition drive in central Delhi. Police are trying to identify the miscreants who engaged in stone-pelting. The demolition was carried out by MCD to remove illegal constructions around the Faiz-e-Ilahi Mosque in the Turkman Gate area.

Article Title: Laxmi Nagar assault: New clip shows SUV crashing into house; accused Omkar Yadav claims self-defence in viral video
Article Text: NEW DELHI: Another CCTV clip related to the Laxmi Nagar assault has surfaced, showing a group of men arriving first, opening a gate and assaulting a man. Moments later, a Thar SUV was seen speeding towards the house and crashing into the wall, after which several men got out of it and the assault continued. Meanwhile, accused Omkar Yadav has released a video on social media defending his brother, gym caretaker and key accused Satish Yadav alias Pintu Yadav.A dispute over a gym operating from a residential property in east Delhi's Laxmi Nagar allegedly escalated into the assault recently when the man was beaten up, his wife was said to be molested, and their son was stripped and assaulted on the street.The man runs a gym from the basement of his house and caretaker Yadav allegedly cheated him and attempted to take over the business, leading to the dispute. On Jan 2, during an argument over a basement- and sewage-related issue, Yadav, along with his associates, assaulted the couple and their son, a senior officer said.An earlier CCTV footage had shown the couple's son being dragged onto the road, stripped and beaten up by a group of four-five men. The presence of police personnel in parts of the footage also raised questions. Police claimed the assault stopped after they arrived while the victims alleged that they were beaten up in full view of the cops, a claim that is being verified.According to the complaint, the couple's son came out after hearing the commotion and was assaulted. The couple also said their two sons had left the house following the attack.Police said main accused Yadav was arrested while the other accused were absconding. Omkar, one of the absconding accused, posted a video on social media, saying his brother had been working with the complainant for "20-25 years" and was running the gym for the past "12-13 years". He questioned why objections over the gym were raised only in the past five-six months. "If we captured the land, why did she start complaining only now?" he asked.Omkar further alleged that the legal proceedings were "one-sided" and claimed that he was also being targeted. He identified himself as a worker of a party and alleged that he was being defamed by an opposition party.Referring to the incident, Omkar said, "On Jan 2, I got a call from my brother. I reached the spot after 10-15 minutes. If I am seen kicking two or three times in the video, it was in self-defence. They started hitting first."A case has been registered at the Laxmi Nagar police station under various provisions of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, including voluntarily causing hurt, wrongful restraint, criminal trespass, assault or use of criminal force to outrage the modesty of a woman, acts intended to insult a woman's modesty and criminal intimidation.
Article Summary: A dispute over a gym operating from a residential property in east Delhi's Laxmi Nagar allegedly escalated into the assault. The man runs a gym from the basement of his house and caretaker Yadav allegedly cheated him and attempted to take over the business. On Jan 2, during an argument over a basement- and sewage- related issue, Yadav along with his associates, assaulted the couple and their son.

Article Title: Multiple Delhi schools receive bomb threats; security tightened
Article Text:
(This is a developing story)





NEW DELHI: Several schools across Delhi received bomb threat messages, prompting authorities to launch security checks on the premises, officials said on Monday.The Delhi Police said all safety protocols are being followed and a thorough inspection of the affected school campuses is underway."So far, nothing suspicious has been found," police officials told news agency ANI, adding that teams are continuing their checks as a precautionary measure.Authorities have stepped up security measures and are monitoring the situation to ensure the safety of students, staff and visitors.
Article Summary: Several schools across Delhi receive bomb threat messages. Authorities launch security checks on the premises. Delhi Police said all safety protocols are being followed. So far, nothing suspicious has been found, police officials said in a statement. The incident is being treated as a precaution.

Article Title: 'Criminal elements in crowd': Delhi Police warning to CJP during Jantar Mantar protest; watch video
Article Text:
A viral video circulating online shows senior Delhi Police officers raising concerns with Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) organisers.

CJP meeting on 5th August





NEW DELHI: A viral video from Delhi's Jantar Mantar has shown senior Delhi Police officers telling Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) organisers that they had failed to make adequate arrangements to manage crowds during the outfit's anti-NEET paper leak protest.According to the video, senior police officers are seen speaking to CJP spokespersons, Ashutosh Ranka and Saurabh Das, saying Jantar Mantar was not meant for protests of that scale without proper planning.The officers say the organisers had not deployed enough volunteers to regulate the gathering despite repeated requests from the police.One officer says he had repeatedly urged the organisers to take action, warning that "criminal elements" were present among the crowd and emphasising the need to deploy volunteers to help maintain order.The officers say they had raised these concerns with the organisers on July 19 and July 20, when attendance at the protest was increasing. They add that they repeatedly cautioned the organisers that the crowd could become difficult to control if adequate arrangements were not made.Meanwhile, CJP's core committee is scheduled to meet at founder Abhijeet Dipke's residence in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar on August 5, according to sources.Sources said party activists and volunteers had been asked to spend time with their families after the conclusion of the month-long protest. Core members were also told to gather feedback from volunteers and students before attending the meeting.The outfit is expected to hold a press conference after the meeting to announce its future strategy.Dipke also met students, local residents and visitors at his residence on Sunday and celebrated Friendship Day with children, sources said.The CJP's protest over the NEET paper leak gained significant traction among young people across the country and culminated in Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation last week.
Article Summary: Viral video shows senior Delhi Police officers raising concerns with Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) organisers. Officers say organisers had not deployed enough volunteers to regulate the gathering. CJP's core committee is scheduled to meet at founder Abhijeet Dipke's residence in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar.

Article Title: 2 killed after house roof collapses in Delhi's Jaiprakash Nagar
Article Text:
(With agency inputs)





NEW DELHI: A couple was killed after the roof of a house collapsed in Delhi's JP Nagar area, officials said on Monday.The incident took place in the Jaiprakash Nagar area of Usmanpur in North-East Delhi on Sunday night.According to officials, the victims were identified as Tinku (32) and his wife, Urmila (30).Both were rescued from the rubble by local residents and police personnel following the collapse.The couple was rushed to Jag Pravesh Hospital, where doctors declared them dead. CMO Dr Santosh confirmed the deaths, according to STO Sunil Sagar.The roof collapse triggered panic among residents, with locals rushing to help those trapped under the debris.Police teams reached the spot and began rescue operations.The exact reason behind the roof collapse is yet to be ascertained.Authorities are expected to conduct an inquiry into the incident.
Article Summary: The incident took place in the Jaiprakash Nagar area of Usmanpur in North-East Delhi. The victims were identified as Tinku (32) and his wife, Urmila (30) Both were rescued from the rubble by local residents and police personnel.

Article Title: 20-year-old drowns while fishing in Nalasopara Lake
Article Text: Nalasopara: A 20-year-old man drowned after slipping into a lake while fishing with his friends in Nalasopara East on Sunday afternoon. The deceased was identified as Sohel Ibrahim Shaikh (20), a resident of Gala Nagar in Nalasopara East.According to officials, Sohel had gone fishing with his friends at Nagela Lake in Shirdi Sankhyeshwar Nagar area when he allegedly lost his footing and fell into the water. After he failed to resurface, his companions alerted the authorities.A team from Achole fire station of Vasai-Virar City Municipal Corporation launched a search operation and later recovered his body from the lake.Meanwhile, local residents alleged that repeated demands for safety measures, including a protective boundary wall, warning signboards and other safeguards around the lake, have been ignored by the civic administration.With rivers, lakes and other water bodies overflowing due to the ongoing monsoon, police have prohibited swimming and recreational activities at such locations, warning residents to stay away from water bodies to prevent accidents.
Article Summary: The deceased was identified as Sohel Ibrahim Shaikh (20), a resident of Gala Nagar in Nalasopara East. Local residents alleged that repeated demands for safety measures, including a protective boundary wall, warning signboards and other safeguards around the lake, have been ignored.

Article Title: 24-year-old Mumbai youth drowns in Karjat river
Article Text: Navi Mumbai: A Wadala youth, Arman Ansari (24), drowned in a river off Solanpada dam, Karjat, on Saturday. A five-member group had arrived at the river on a picnic. Ansari had jumped from a bundh into the water to swim but hit his head and chin on the underwater rock surface before drowning.The victim remained missing deep in the water. His friends screamed for assistance. Hours later he was swept away several metres downstream. The locals arrived at the dam to rescue the victim in response to the SOS call of his friends.The locals started searching for him. The body of Ansari was noticed stuck underneath a bridge over the river. The locals pulled him out of the water, joining hands with four of his other friends. The victim was rushed to the sub-district hospital, Karjat.After a post-mortem, his body was handed over to his relatives. An accidental death case has been filed with Karjat police station. Further investigation is on.Ansari is originally from Uttar Pradesh. Entry to the dam has been restricted, according to locals. However, monsoon revellers are flocking to rivers, check dams and other spots for enjoyment.
Article Summary: Arman Ansari, 24, drowned in a river off Solanpada dam, Karjat, on Saturday. Ansari had jumped from a bundh into the water to swim but hit his head and chin on the underwater rock surface before drowning.

Article Title: Villagers oppose public hearing on stone quarries for Vadhvan Port Project in Maharashtra
Article Text: Palghar: A public hearing conducted by Maharashtra Pollution Control Board (MPCB) on Sunday for the proposed environmental clearance of stone quarry projects at Gargaon in Palghar district witnessed strong opposition from local villagers and environmental activists. Despite the protests, the hearing was completed under heavy police security.The proposed quarries at Gargaon and Khaniwade in Boisar are intended to supply rock for the land reclamation works of the proposed Vadhvan Port Project Limited (VPPL). As part of the environmental clearance process, the MPCB organised a public hearing at Shigav-Khutad village in Boisar.Hundreds of villagers gathered outside the venue and staged a sit-in protest, alleging that the hearing was being conducted without adequately addressing their concerns over the project’s environmental and social impact.Vinit Patil of the Vadhvan Port Virodhi Sangharsh Samiti said the environmental impact assessment (EIA) report had been prepared only in English and had not been provided to the concerned gram panchayats in a language understood by local residents.Shigav sarpanch Dipti Sumda said local communities had already parted with land for the port project and would now face further displacement and environmental degradation due to large-scale quarrying.“The government should source the stone from elsewhere instead of destroying our villages,” she said.Another villager, Bharat Vayeda, demanded that the hearing be postponed, stating that many residents were unable to attend as they were engaged in agricultural work during the ongoing farming season.Despite the objections, officials proceeded with the public hearing amid tight police deployment. According to Maharashtra Pollution Control Board, 232 villagers attended the hearing.
Article Summary: The proposed quarries at Gargaon and Khaniwade in Boisar are intended to supply rock for the land reclamation works of the proposed Vadhvan Port Project Limited. Hundreds of villagers gathered outside the venue and staged a sit-in protest. Despite the protests, the hearing was completed under heavy police security.

Article Title: Unidentified woman’s body washes ashore at Arnala beach in Maharashtra
Article Text: Virar: The body of an unidentified woman was found washed ashore at Arnala beach near Virar on Sunday morning, prompting police to launch an investigation into the cause of her death.According to the police, the woman is believed to be between 25 and 30 years old, and her identity is yet to be established. After conducting an inquest, the body was sent to hospital for a post-mortem examination. Police said the exact cause of death remains unknown and all possible angles, including murder, suicide and accidental drowning, are being investigated. Officials said the post-mortem report is expected to provide clarity on the circumstances surrounding the woman’s death.An accidental death case has been registered at the Arnala Sagari Police Station, and efforts are underway to identify the deceased.As part of the investigation, police are verifying records of missing women from nearby police stations and have also shared details with police units in neighbouring districts.
Article Summary: The body of an unidentified woman was found washed ashore at Arnala beach near Virar on Sunday morning. Police said the exact cause of death remains unknown and all possible angles, including murder, suicide and accidental drowning, are being investigated. An accidental death case has been registered at the Arnala Sagari Police Station.
